title: Optical linewidth narrowing for device-coupled single T centers
authors: Adam Johnston, Yu-En Wong, Shengbin Yan, Ulises Felix-Rendon, Songtao Chen
abstract: Single T centers in silicon have emerged as promising optically active spins for quantum networking applications. One of the major obstacles to advancing the system is their broad optical linewidth due to spectral diffusion, which is two orders of magnitude larger than their cavity-enhanced radiative linewidth. We tackle this issue by utilizing above-band optical excitation delivered via a laser scanning microscope to device-coupled single T centers, achieving up to 70% optical linewidth reduction. We attribute the linewidth narrowing effect to the filling of nearby charge traps by photo-generated free carriers. We analyze charge stabilization dynamics by exploiting pulsed above-band excitation and develop a rate equation model to describe the dynamics and to explain the observed linewidth narrowing and center shift. This work provides an effective pathway to control and reduce the optical linewidth for single T centers, clearing one of the major roadblocks to advance the single T center spin platform for quantum information and networking applications.
summary: The paper addresses the critical issue of broad optical linewidth in silicon T centers by employing above-band laser excitation. By analyzing the resulting charge stabilization dynamics using rate equations and spectroscopy, the authors successfully demonstrated a significant reduction (up to 70%) in this noise-induced linewidth. This work establishes an active control pathway necessary for advancing T centers toward practical quantum information applications.
main_problem: The primary obstacle for using single T centers as quantum emitters is their broad optical linewidth, which severely limits their utility in quantum networking.
main_result: The authors demonstrated an effective method to achieve up to 70% reduction in the optical linewidth by utilizing above-band optical excitation.
method: They combined time-resolved Photoluminescence Excitation (PLE) spectroscopy with controlled above-band laser pumping and developed a rate equation model to describe charge stabilization dynamics.
model_or_system: The system involves single T centers in silicon coupled to nanophotonic waveguides. The physics is modeled by considering the filling of nearby charge traps by photo-generated free carriers, which stabilizes the local electric field environment.
key_observables:
Optical linewidth ($\Gamma$), center frequency shift ($\Delta
u$), trap filling probability ($p$), and time constants for charge dynamics.
important_parameters: Above-band excitation power ($P_{AB}$), laser wavelength ($\lambda_{AB} < 	ext{bandgap}$), and characteristic decay time constants (e.g., $41 \pm 2.6$ ns).
main_assumptions: The linewidth narrowing is directly attributed to the neutralization effect caused by photo-generated free carriers filling nearby charge traps, which reduces spectral diffusion noise.
figures_summary: Figures show PLE spectra confirming single emitters and demonstrate that increasing above-band power ($P_{AB}$) systematically narrows the linewidth and causes a measurable frequency shift. Time evolution plots track these changes over time delays.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from initial characterization (broad linewidth) to demonstrating the effect of controlled excitation, quantifying the reduction via spectroscopy, developing rate equations for charge dynamics, and finally modeling the resulting spectral narrowing and shifts.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, experimentally verifiable mechanism—charge trap filling via above-band pumping—to actively suppress spectral diffusion noise in solid-state qubits, which is crucial knowledge for designing robust quantum memory nodes.
